SMTO-HTTP-0043 — SMTO couldn't sign in to the service

GUID: eadd2f7b-e6c1-4349-9e3b-5c1352df7d7a
Slug: http-auth-failed
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • Signing in to the service failed, but this message comes from an older, general label that doesn't say which part of the sign-in went wrong.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection the task uses, and select Test connection. The test runs the sign-in again and usually reports a more specific problem.
  2. Follow what the test reports. If it points to the sign-in details, re-enter them under Authentication and save. This old message can't say which part failed, but the new test result can.
  3. When the test shows Authenticated, run the task again. That confirms the sign-in works before the task tries again.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the test result, to the person who manages SMTO or the service account. Never paste passwords, keys or tokens into a task, chat message, screenshot or the details you share.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A legacy http_auth_failed kind was reported; recovery classification recognizes it, but no current producer narrows the cause.

What this means

  • This retained authentication-failure kind is recognized by recovery classification but has no direct current producer establishing a narrower cause. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • This retained authentication-failure kind is recognized by recovery classification but has no direct current producer establishing a narrower cause.

How to diagnose it

  • Use the accompanying status, phase and safe authentication evidence; do not guess a mapping or credential defect.

How to fix it

  • Re-run the connection test to obtain a specific authentication error and act on that; inspect the auth endpoint status and response in the Run activity or Gateway log rather than changing credentials blindly.
  • Inspect the specific authentication evidence and correct only its established cause.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual failure boundary is identified and its supported authentication check passes.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
